findings.title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed on restart
findings.body: The flusher creates processes via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose type is SpawnProcess. The restart path guards cleanup with isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), where multiprocessing.Process is the default-context (fork) Process class on Linux and is not a base class of SpawnProcess, so the check is False. As a result when _ensure_processes_alive detects a dead/hung process it calls _create_process_for_shards without killing the old process. A hung process keeps flushing the same Redis shards while the replacement also flushes them, causing duplicate Kafka produces, Redis contention, fd/pid leaks and unbounded process growth. The same isinstance guard in join() prevents terminate() of hung spawn processes on shutdown.

findings.title: Zero/negative process count crashes or disables flushing
findings.body: num_processes is computed as min(max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) where max_processes is max_processes or len(...). If assigned_shards is empty on rebalance, or max_processes is 0/negative, num_processes becomes 0 or negative. That yields an empty process_to_shards_map and then i % self.num_processes raises ZeroDivisionError for 0, or i % -1 returns 0 and raises KeyError because the map is empty. With 0 processes submit/record/backpressure loops become no-ops so segments are never flushed, causing silent data loss instead of a clear startup error.

findings.title: --flusher-processes accepts invalid values that crash consumer
findings.body: The new --flusher-processes click Option defaults to 1 with type=int and no range validation, so 0 or negative values are accepted and passed as max_processes to SpanFlusher. In the flusher that leads to zero/negative num_processes, which crashes with ZeroDivisionError/KeyError or silently creates no flusher processes. The CLI should reject values <1.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards
findings.body: The produce timer is emitted with tags={"shard": shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag} for the same shard-group value. Consumers of metrics querying by one tag name will miss the other, breaking dashboards and alerts for flusher produce latency.

findings.title: Mocked sleep makes flush wait a no-op, test is racy
findings.body: The test replaces time.sleep with lambda _: None, then after advancing current_drift calls time.sleep(0.1) intending to give background flusher threads time to flush. Because sleep is mocked the wait does nothing. join() sets stopped=True immediately, so whether the flusher flushes before exiting is a race. The test can flakily pass/fail and does not deterministically verify multiprocessed flushing.
